title: Gezer calendar, Istanbul 2089 T
language: Hebrew (square script and transliteration, Lidzbarski/Driver 1913) / English (Driver 1913)
source: Gezer tablet, Istanbul 2089 T: Driver 1913 Plate I (public domain) and a Commons photograph (CC BY-SA 4.0) + Driver's 1913 text and translation (public domain)
description: The Gezer calendar (about 10th century BCE), seven lines naming the months of the farming year, with Lidzbarski's reading and Driver's 1913 translation and photographs of the tablet.
introduction:
The Gezer calendar is a small tablet of soft limestone, about 11 cm high, found in 1908 by R. A. S. Macalister in his excavations at Gezer for the Palestine Exploration Fund. Its seven short lines list the months of the farming year by their work: ingathering, sowing, late sowing, cutting flax, barley harvest, the general harvest, pruning the vines and summer fruit. It is usually dated to about the 10th century BCE, and it is one of the oldest known inscriptions in a language close to the Hebrew of the Old Testament; the tablet may have been a writing exercise. It is now in the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (inv. 2089 T).

The text is Mark Lidzbarski's reading as printed by S. R. Driver in 1913, in Hebrew square letters, with a letter-for-letter Latin transliteration of the same text and Driver's English. Driver's printed errata are applied (lines 3 and 5 begin ירח, not ירחו). A line over a letter marks an uncertain reading. The letters written apart at the lower left corner, which Lidzbarski read as the beginning of a name, are not part of the seven lines given here.
translator_notes: Driver's line over a letter means 'the reading is not quite certain' (Notes, p. viii, note 2).
Driver on line 4: 'The ם is placed below the line for want of space.'
The Latin transliteration is a mechanical letter-for-letter rendering of the square-script text (ʾ b g d h w z ḥ ṭ y k l m n s ʿ p ṣ q r š t); it adds no reading of its own.

translation.original_text: 1 ירחו אסף ירחו ז̅1 yrḥw ʾsp yrḥw z̅2 רע ירחו לקש2 rʿ yrḥw lqš3 ירח עצד פשת3 yrḥ ʿṣd pšt4 ירח קצר שערם4 yrḥ qṣr šʿrm5 ירח קצרו כל5 yrḥ qṣrw kl6 ירחו זמר6 yrḥw zmr7 ירח קץ7 yrḥ qṣ
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>The month of ingathering [Tishri]. The month of <sup>2</sup>sowing. The month of late sowing. <sup>3</sup>The month of cutting (or hoeing up ?) flax. <sup>4</sup>The month of barley-harvest. <sup>5</sup>The month of the general harvest. <sup>6</sup>The month of (vine-)pruning. <sup>7</sup>The month of summer-fruits.
translation.scan_note: All seven lines are on the one inscribed face, which both photographs show whole (checked on the images: seven lines of large incised letters under the broken top edge, read right to left; line 1 begins at the right with yrḥw, the circle of ʿayin stands near the right end of line 2 in rʿ, and the last two lines are short; a few letters are written apart at the lower left corner). The first image is the photographic plate in Driver's book (1913), the second a recent photograph in Istanbul. Line numbers are Driver's.
